summary: All three game-flow items are fixed. rules-01: an uncharged crossing of the human's own trail (LassoCrossNoCharge, R8 and R16 unchanged) now arms a one-time lesson that the next UNCHASED return shows as the bubble tut.selfcross for 4.0 s of visible time, without a pointer. Priority is Cut > Lasso > SelfCross > Exit. A chased return drops the lesson, a new exit cancels a pending one, and SparkCaught or Eliminated cancel both. It is saved as SaveData.TutSelfCrossDone. rules-05: the tutorial lesson timers advance only while the bubble is really on screen (TutorialOverlay.CountsAsVisible: wanted, shown and alpha >= 0.95), so time behind the pause panel, in the ready gate after a pause or in the death beat no longer uses up the 2.5 s first-cut lesson. The chased-return path is unchanged. robust-04: GameDirector.SleepTimeoutFor gives NeverSleep only while Playing and not paused. It is applied on every change of IsPaused (SetPaused both ways, ForceUnpause), so the pause panel, including after an automatic pause, lets the screen sleep. On Android without -fps, the frame rate is 30 while paused and goes back to 60 at unpause, StartRound and ToMenu (ApplyTargetFrameRate, which never re-runs the renderScale lines). Windows stays on vSync. Two deliberate deviations from the plan text, both for the player: (1) TutSelfCrossDone is saved once the bubble has been visible for 2.5 s (the same rule as the cut lesson) instead of when it starts; (2) a new Exit hides an active self-crossing bubble only after those 2.5 s, because the 23.3 edge flicker raises Exit events along the territory border and a quick new excursion would otherwise blink the lesson away before it can be read. A pending lesson is still cancelled by any Exit, as the plan says. The overlay is now driven through TickCore(dt, TickInputs), and Tick reads the live inputs, so EditMode tests can drive the real overlay without a GameDirector. SaveData gained a test-only MemoryOnly scope so tests can set flags without writing PlayerPrefs. Verified on my build Build/game-flow: 16 new EditMode tests green; the full EditMode run is 484/486 green, and the 2 failures are in other packages' in-progress WaveC test files. PlayMode is 8/8 green (BootTests and SteeringInputPlayTests). Probe -biome liquid -fps 30: [ProbeResult] PASS, [ProbeHash] 246577239DE179C4 (sim unchanged). DevShot with -uidemo selfcross was checked in FR (liquid) and EN (fire) at 540x960, and the cut bubble correctly takes priority in the CutDroplets shot.

items.evidence: SaveData.TutSelfCrossDone (key pio.TutSelfCrossDone, cached, invalidated in ReloadCache like the other Tut flags; there is no tutorial reset path in the project). Strings key tut.selfcross FR 'Recroiser ton fil ouvre ta boucle : rentre sans le recroiser pour tout peindre.' EN 'Crossing your own thread breaks the loop: come home without crossing it to paint it all.' TutorialOverlay: Bubble.SelfCross with selfCrossPending/Shown/Active/Time (+ selfCrossDone), reset in Bind; OnSimEvent handles LassoCrossNoCharge, Return (chased: drop; unchased: start), Exit, SparkCaught and Eliminated; Tick priority Cut > Lasso > SelfCross > Exit; 4.0 s of visible time; no pointer; SetBubbleText maps SelfCross to tut.selfcross. Tests (all green, TestResults/game-flow_edit.xml): WaveC_SelfCross_UnchasedReturnAfterAnUnchargedCrossingShowsTheBubbleOnce, WaveC_SelfCross_ChasedReturnShowsNothing, WaveC_SelfCross_SavedFlagSuppressesTheLesson, WaveC_SelfCross_ABotCrossingDoesNothing, WaveC_SelfCross_AnExitBetweenTheCrossingAndTheReturnCancelsIt, WaveC_SelfCross_SparkCatchAndEliminationCancelIt, WaveC_SelfCross_ANewExitHidesTheBubbleOnlyOnceItWasRead, WaveC_SelfCross_PriorityBelowCutAndLasso, WaveC_SelfCross_TimerStopsWhileTheBubbleIsHidden, WaveC_Strings_SelfCrossLineInBothLanguages, WaveC_SaveData_TutSelfCrossDoneIsCachedWithoutWritingPlayerPrefsInMemoryOnlyMode; Strings_EveryKeyExistsInBothTables and Strings_ValuesAreNonEmptyWithoutEmDashAndWithMatchingPlaceholders green. Player screenshots (bubble forced with -uidemo selfcross, layout check): docs/waveC/game-flow/selfcross_fr_liquid/liquid_MidFill.png (3 lines, fits the 880 px bubble), docs/waveC/game-flow/selfcross_en_fire/fire_MidFill.png (3 lines), docs/waveC/game-flow/selfcross_fr_liquid/liquid_CutDroplets.png (the cut bubble and its pointer win over SelfCross). Deviations from the plan text: the saved flag is written after 2.5 s of visible time, not when the bubble starts; an Exit hides the active bubble only after those 2.5 s.

TutorialOverlay.TickCore computes want and shown first, then advances cutVisible only when want == Cut and CountsAsVisible(shown, want, bubbleAlpha) (public static: want != None && shown == want && alpha >= VisibleAlpha 0.95); the same rule drives the SelfCross timer. Return with Chased -> MarkCutDone unchanged. Tests: WaveC_CountsAsVisible_OnlyWhenWantedShownAndFadedIn; WaveC_CutLesson_HiddenTimeNeverCounts (a non-persisting session with SaveData.MemoryOnly: 3 s paused, 3 s in the ready gate and 3 s in the death beat leave CutVisibleSeconds at 0, CutLessonDone false and SaveData.TutCutDone false; then 1 s on screen is not enough and 2.5 s really on screen completes it); WaveC_CutLesson_ChasedReturnStillMarksItDone. A real paused GameDirector cannot be built in EditMode (Awake does not run), so the director-derived booleans are passed through TutorialOverlay.TickInputs to the same TickCore that Tick uses. PlayMode Pause_ReadyGateAndSlowMo is green.

GameDirector.SleepTimeoutFor(GameState, bool paused) returns NeverSleep only for Playing and not paused. It returns int because Unity's SleepTimeout is a class of int constants, not an enum. ApplySleepTimeout uses it and runs from SetState and from the new ApplyPauseSettings, which SetPaused (both directions) and ForceUnpause call. Android only (#if UNITY_ANDROID && !UNITY_EDITOR): ApplyTargetFrameRate(paused) sets Application.targetFrameRate = AndroidTargetFrameRate(LaunchArgs.Fps, paused), which is the -fps value when given, else 30 paused and 60 otherwise. It is called from ApplyFrameSettings (in place of the old line; the renderScale lines are untouched and never re-run), ApplyPauseSettings and SetSession (StartRound, ToMenu). Windows keeps vSync. The QualityTier watchdog already ignores paused and ready-gate frames, so the 30 fps pause cannot trigger a false tier step. Tests: WaveC_SleepTimeoutFor_NeverSleepOnlyWhilePlayingAndNotPaused (Playing and Menu, paused and not, plus Results and Boot), WaveC_AndroidTargetFrameRate_ThirtyWhilePausedUnlessFpsIsGiven; RuntimeSkeletonTests 9/9 and PlayMode BootTests 4/4 green. Pending for the gate: the Android branch compiles only in BuildAndroid, which game-flow did not run to keep the shared lock free, and the screen-sleep / 30 fps behaviour needs the device playtest.

api_additions: TutorialOverlay.Bubble (public enum None, Exit, Cut, Lasso, SelfCross; was private), TutorialOverlay.TickInputs (struct: Live, HumanAlive, HumanHasSpark, AwaitingStart, Paused, InBeat), TutorialOverlay.TickCore(float dt, TickInputs k) (Tick = TickCore(dt, live inputs))

TutorialOverlay.CountsAsVisible(Bubble shown, Bubble want, float alpha) (public static, not internal: the project has no InternalsVisibleTo for the test assembly), constants SelfCrossSeconds = 4, SelfCrossDoneSeconds = 2.5, VisibleAlpha = 0.95
TutorialOverlay read-only state for tests: WantedBubble, ShownBubble, CutLessonDone, CutVisibleSeconds, SelfCrossPending, SelfCrossLessonDone
SaveData.MemoryOnly (tests only: setters update the cache and raise Changed without writing PlayerPrefs, Flush is a no-op; every change of the value drops the cache)
GameDirector.SleepTimeoutFor(GameState state, bool paused) -> int, GameDirector.AndroidTargetFrameRate(int fpsArg, bool paused) -> int, constants AndroidFrameRate = 60 and AndroidPausedFrameRate = 30
Dev aid: '-uidemo selfcross' forces the self-crossing bubble during play (screenshots only, like '-uidemo hint')
contract_issues: 15.4 gains a step: 'After the human crossed its own trail without a charge (LassoCrossNoCharge; nothing is shown at the crossing itself), the first UNCHASED return shows the bubble tut.selfcross (Recroiser ton fil ouvre ta boucle : rentre sans le recroiser pour tout peindre. / Crossing your own thread breaks the loop: come home without crossing it to paint it all.) for 4.0 s of visible time, without pointer, priority Cut > Lasso > SelfCross > Exit. A chased return drops the pending lesson; a new exit cancels a pending lesson and hides the bubble once it has been visible for 2.5 s; SparkCaught and Eliminated cancel both. SaveData.TutSelfCrossDone = true once the bubble stayed visible for 2.5 s. Never repeated once the flag is set, at most once per round.'

15.4 (TutCutDone): 'the bubble stayed visible for >= 2.5 s of real time' now means wanted (not paused, not in the ready gate, not in the death beat), its text shown and faded in (alpha >= 0.95); time behind the pause panel, in the ready gate after a pause or in the death beat does not count.

11.5 gains 'public static bool TutSelfCrossDone { get; set; }' (and the test-only 'public static bool MemoryOnly { get; set; }'); the consumers line: TutorialOverlay reads and writes the four Tut flags.

11.1: 'Screen.sleepTimeout = SleepTimeout.NeverSleep while Playing and not paused, SleepTimeout.SystemSetting otherwise (the pause panel, also after an automatic pause, lets the screen sleep); on Android without -fps, Application.targetFrameRate = 30 while paused, 60 restored when the pause ends (and at StartRound / ToMenu).'
15.6: new key tut.selfcross in both tables.

Fix plan wording: CountsAsVisible and SleepTimeoutFor are public static rather than internal static (no InternalsVisibleTo exists for PainterIO.Tests.EditMode), and SleepTimeoutFor returns int (Unity's SleepTimeout is a class of int constants, not an enum).
